title: Non-blocking finding from frontend-daily-homework-history-followups-followups' PR review (#404)
description: pr-reviewer's full review of PR #404 (frontend-daily-homework-history-followups-followups) accepted it -- make e2e (28/28, plus a mutation test that temporarily broke the History table's date rendering to confirm the assertion is still load-bearing), static analysis, and coverage all passed, and the waitForResponse-vs-click ordering was verified correct (listener registered before the triggering click via Promise.all, not after). One non-blocking test-infrastructure-convention finding surfaced and shouldn't disappear once PR #404 merges.

checklist.step: frontend/tests/e2e/daily-homework.spec.ts now imports directly from `../../src/api/homework` (a type) and `../../src/utils/format` (a value) -- the first e2e spec in frontend/tests/e2e/ to import anything from `src/` at all; every other spec that needs a shared helper (e.g. portfolio.spec.ts's `isoDateWeeksAgo`) imports it from `tests/dateFixtures.ts` instead, a tests-local module, not application source. This import is correct and was the right fix for the specific duplication finding it closed (the task's checklist explicitly called for importing `formatDate` directly), but it's a new precedent: an e2e spec now has a compile-time dependency on an app-source module's exact path/export shape, which couples a black-box browser-level test to an internal refactor in a way the rest of the suite doesn't. Worth an explicit, recorded convention decision for future specs -- e.g. should an e2e spec import src/ helpers directly when there's no real alternative (as here), or should a shared tests/-local re-export/wrapper be preferred to keep that coupling at one boundary -- rather than leaving it as an ad hoc one-off that future spec authors might copy inconsistently.

decisions.decision: Documented an explicit convention in docs/architecture/Testing.md's "End-to-end (Playwright)" section: an e2e spec may import a *type* or a *pure, side-effect-free utility/formatting function* directly from `src/` (both tsconfigs already cover `src` and `tests` together) when that's needed to assert against the exact value/format the app itself produces -- e.g. daily-homework.spec.ts's `DailyHomeworkOut` type (import type, erased at compile time, zero runtime coupling) and `formatDate` (src/utils/format.ts, a pure function with no React/DOM/app-state dependency). Importing a React component, hook, context, or any module with side effects/DOM/app-runtime dependencies is not allowed, to keep the suite's black-box (real browser, real DOM) boundary intact. A genuinely test-only need shared across specs that isn't a copy/wrapper of app logic (e.g. isoDateWeeksAgo) still belongs in a tests/-local module (tests/dateFixtures.ts), not under src/. Added a short comment to daily-homework.spec.ts itself pointing back to this convention for discoverability. No code change to the spec's imports was needed -- both of its existing src/ imports (a type-only import and a pure utility) already conform to the convention as decided.
decisions.rationale: Rejected two alternatives. (1) Banning all direct src/ imports and requiring every such need to go through a tests/-local re-export/wrapper module: for a type import this adds pure ceremony since a type is erased at compile time and carries zero runtime coupling risk, so wrapping it in a tests/-local re-export doesn't reduce any real coupling, only adds indirection. For a pure value like `formatDate`, a tests/-local wrapper would still have to import it from src/ internally to stay correct -- it relocates where the src/ dependency is declared without removing it, and risks the wrapper itself drifting out of sync with the real helper the way the prior ad hoc inline reimplementation already did (the exact bug frontend-daily-homework-history-followups-followups fixed by importing the real helper instead of recreating its logic). Importing the real helper directly is what makes the assertion catch genuine app-formatting drift; a wrapper doesn't add that property, it only costs a layer of indirection. (2) Allowing unrestricted src/ imports with no scope limit: rejected because the whole reason this suite exists (per Testing.md's own framing) is to catch disagreement between app code and its own mocked test doubles by driving the real browser/DOM -- a spec that could import and exercise a component or hook directly would let a future spec bypass the browser-level black-box boundary entirely, re-introducing the exact class of gap the mocked unit/component suites and this e2e suite are supposed to catch independently of each other. Scoping the exception to type-only and pure-value imports keeps that boundary intact while still permitting the one case (comparing against the app's actual formatting logic) that genuinely needs it. isoDateWeeksAgo was kept as the precedent for the tests/-local case specifically because it's test-fixture logic that doesn't exist in app source at all (not a copy or wrapper of anything in src/), so there's no inconsistency in treating it differently from formatDate/DailyHomeworkOut.

comments.summary: The new src/-import convention in Testing.md is documentary only -- no eslint rule (e.g. a tests/e2e/**-scoped no-restricted-imports override) mechanically enforces the type-only/pure-function boundary, so a future spec importing a component/hook in violation of the rule wouldn't be caught by lint, only by a reviewer reading the diff. The worked example and explicit prohibition make the common case reasonably clear, but a borderline helper (one with a non-obvious transitive dependency) is inherently a human judgment call under this convention as written. Non-blocking; tracked as a follow-up.

Minor documentation-accuracy nit: the new paragraph says the exception works because "both tsconfig.app.json and Playwright's own tsconfig already include src and tests together" -- there is no separate Playwright-specific tsconfig file in frontend/ (confirmed by search); Playwright's runner transpiles specs without type-checking them, and type-checking happens solely via tsc -b --noEmit against the one tsconfig.app.json, which already covers src/tests/.storybook. The phrasing implies a second config that doesn't exist. Non-blocking; tracked as a follow-up.

review.notes:
Full review of PR #405 (frontend-daily-homework-history-followups-followups-followups), a decision-and-document task with no application-code changes: a new convention paragraph in docs/architecture/Testing.md's End-to-end (Playwright) section, a discoverability comment added to tests/e2e/daily-homework.spec.ts, and task-board bookkeeping (decisions entry, checklist flip, git block) on this task plus the index.json mirror.

Independent verification performed: (1) Read the full Testing.md diff -- the convention is clearly stated, correctly placed under the existing End-to-end (Playwright) section, gives a concrete worked example (DailyHomeworkOut as import type, formatDate as a pure function) and an explicit prohibition (no component/hook/context/anything with app-runtime or DOM dependencies), and doesn't contradict anything else in Testing.md or docs/architecture/Frontend.md -- grepped both for any conflicting src/-import or e2e-boundary language, found none. (2) Grepped the whole of frontend/tests/e2e/ for any import from src/: only daily-homework.spec.ts has one (the DailyHomeworkOut type import and the formatDate import, both already present pre-PR), confirming the claim that it already conforms and that no other spec violates the newly-written rule on day one. Also confirmed tests/renderWithProviders.tsx, tests/renderWithTheme.tsx, and tests/mocks/handlers.ts do import from src/, but none of those are e2e specs (they're vitest/mocked-suite fixtures the new convention doesn't govern) -- not a violation. (3) Own assessment of the convention's enforceability: the type-only/pure-function boundary is reasonably checkable for the worked example and most realistic cases (no React/DOM/app-state dependency is a clear bright line), but there is no automated backstop (no scoped eslint no-restricted-imports rule) -- enforcement is entirely reviewer-judgment-based, which is consistent with most other conventions in this repo's docs but still a real, if minor, gap; filed as a non-blocking finding rather than blocking on it, since the project doesn't generally require every documented convention to have a matching lint rule. (4) Re-ran all claimed checks myself rather than trusting the PR description: backend ruff check . and mypy clean; frontend yarn lint and yarn tsc -b --noEmit clean (zero output); python3 scripts/check_profit_target_wording.py clean; python3 scripts/validate_tasks.py -- validated 385 task files, no violations; make e2e -- 28/28 specs passed; backend pytest --cov=app -- 1618 passed, 99.94% coverage; frontend vitest run --coverage -- 99.78%/99.05%/99.84%/99.81% statements/branches/functions/lines. All numbers match the PR description's claims exactly. (5) UI-facing-work check: this PR touches no application code a user would click through (docs + a code comment only) -- the browser-walkthrough step (9) is explicitly skipped as not applicable; the persisted e2e suite (step 9a) was still run per the general gate above and passed 28/28. (6) Decision-memory cross-check: the task's own checklist item was phrased as needing "an explicit, recorded convention decision," and the task's decisions array now has exactly that entry with both decision and rationale (including two rejected alternatives) -- satisfies CLAUDE.md's decision-memory rule, no gap. (7) area is frontend/pages, not backend/signals or backend/portfolio, and skill is null, not verify-elder-signal -- verify-elder-signal not applicable. No new module/dependency/layer -- architecture-review not applicable. No API route/schema touched -- openapi.json regeneration not applicable. No new or substantially-changed frontend component -- the common-vs-feature placement check (7a) isn't applicable since nothing component-shaped was added or changed. (8) Also ran the code-review skill (medium effort) against the diff independently; it found zero correctness/reuse/efficiency bugs, consistent with my own read, and separately noticed the same tsconfig-wording imprecision but judged it not concrete enough to raise on its own -- I disagree slightly and am tracking it as a minor non-blocking finding anyway per the "every finding, however minor" rule for follow-up tracking.

Both findings above are minor and documentation-only; neither blocks the accept. Filed as docs/tasks/frontend-daily-homework-history-followups-followups-followups-followups.json (new follow-up task, since none existed for this task id yet) and added to index.json.
